briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Anthropic Claude 4.5 escalate multi-agent capabilities amid rising safety concerns

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs continue rapid iteration on reasoning models while governments accelerate regulatory frameworks. Compute shortages persist despite massive new data center announcements. DialectForge protocol gains traction in enterprise security discussions.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4-preview with 2.3x gains on agentic benchmarks. Anthropic launched Claude 4.5 Opus. Google DeepMind's Gemini 3 and Meta's Llama 4.1 entered testing. xAI deployed Grok-3 and DeepSeek-V4 shipped updates. Multi-agent coordination emerged as the dominant performance driver.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. New NIST guidelines target agentic workflows. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent, automotive, and BCI use cases.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft announced $42B Stargate expansion. TSMC 2nm AI chips entered volume production. Oracle and CoreWeave signed $18B GPU cloud deals. Energy constraints now limit training runs beyond 10^27 FLOPs.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will protocol-level dialect negotiation become mandatory for all frontier multi-agent deployments by 2028?
